ns2:course.label: US Citizenship Comparatively
ns2:course.description: Examines the racial, gendered, and sexualized aspects of US citizenship historically and comparatively. Interdisciplinary course taught from a humanities perspective. Readings draw from critical legal studies, history, literature, literary criticism, and ethnography. Same as AFRO 215, AIS 295, GWS 215, and LLS 215.
ns2:course.courseSectionInformation: Same as AFRO 215, AIS 295, GWS 215, and LLS 215.
ns2:course.sectionDegreeAttributes: Humanities - Hist & Phil, and Cultural Studies - US Minority course.
